title: Week of Nov 30
text: Written Nov 23 from LinkedIn and Instagram posts published Nov 9 to 22 (Supermetrics, through Nov 22): 27 LinkedIn posts, the last on Nov 19, and 27 Instagram posts, the last on Nov 20. Compared with Oct 12 to Nov 8 and with October. Series and programs come from the ATM Kitchen board, refreshed Nov 23. Posts from Nov 18 on are under seven days old, so their numbers will still rise. The two tests set on Nov 16 (LinkedIn openers, Instagram hooks) run to Nov 25 and are read next week. This week's two experiments run Nov 24 to Dec 4.

title: AAF Hall of Achievement cuts draw more than three times ATM's comments per post, and Jennifer Hourigan's drew the most LinkedIn impressions since Oct 7.
text: The 14 AAF Hall of Achievement posts since Oct 20 (7 LinkedIn, 7 Instagram) reached a median 2.0 times their channel's median post and drew 8.6 comments each, against 2.5 across all ATM posts: the most comments per post of any series or program with 10 or more posts. Jennifer Hourigan (Initiative, Nov 16) drew 5,973 LinkedIn impressions and 49 comments, the most impressions since Sharb Farjami on Oct 7 (7,034) and the most comments since the Sara Fischer honoree post of Sep 23 (60). Inductees share these posts in their own words: on 5 of them, those reposts lifted engagement to 2.36 times ATM's own, and Catherine Pinkham Berger's own repost took her 255-impression cut to 12.53 times its organic engagement. The exceptions are the two LinkedIn cuts at half the median, Keri Richardson (251, Oct 26) and Catherine Pinkham Berger (255, Nov 5).

title: With the winner thank-you cuts gone, a week of guest cuts took LinkedIn back to Awards-week impressions without an event.
text: LinkedIn drew 20,367 impressions Nov 16 to 22, twice the 10,320 of Nov 9 to 15 and level with the 20,602 of Moment Awards week (Nov 2 to 8); the weekly average for Oct 12 to Nov 8 was 14,315. New followers rose to 54 (Nov 16 to 21) from 22. Nine of the 12 LinkedIn posts Nov 16 to 19 were guest cuts, with a median of 950 impressions, while 7 of the 15 posts Nov 9 to 12 were winner thank-you cuts, with a median of 407. Across the 14 days, the 15 guest cuts had a median of 949, against 752 for Oct 12 to Nov 8 and 681 in October. Trend Watch (14 posts, 1.4 times the channel median and rising) added Meredith Diehn (goodwipes) at 1,014 impressions and 8 comments; the counter-example is Keri Richardson (CrowdAxis, Nov 18) at 209.

title: Instagram guest reels that tag the guest's own account reached more than twice those that tag only the company, and none of last week's did.
text: The style guide asks every post to tag the person and the company. Of the 39 guest reels Oct 6 to Nov 15, the 5 that tagged the guest's own account had a median reach of 1,001 (Alice Ma 1,442, Kerry Flynn 1,414, Sara Fischer 1,001, Nayeema Raza 651, Charlotte Owen 384); the 34 that tagged only the company, or no one, had a median of 407. None of the 9 guest reels Nov 16 to 20 tagged the guest, and they reached a median 293, though most are under seven days old. At least three of the five tagged reels were also accepted collabs, so the tag and the collab work together. The counter-example is Bridget Evans (Spotify Advertising, Nov 3), who reached 3,216 with only the company tagged.

title: Tag the guest's own Instagram account on every guest reel.
text: For every Instagram guest reel Nov 24 to Dec 4, find the guest's own account before posting and tag it next to the company ("Jennifer Hourigan (@handle) at @initiativeww"). Send the collab invite to the guest's account as well as the company's, and put the accept ask in the live-links email. Where the guest has no public account, log "no account". Keep the hook split running through Nov 25. For each reel, log whether the guest was tagged and whether the collab was accepted.
next_step: Measure: median reach per reel after seven days against 407, the median guest reel that did not tag the guest Oct 6 to Nov 15 (1,001, the five that did, is the stretch). Compare accepted collabs with the rest once November collab status is read.

title: Make the next Instagram Movers & Shakers post a tagged collab with a new first line.
text: Industry Movers & Shakers reaches 0.5 times the channel median over 13 posts, draws 0.3 comments per post and is falling; on Instagram the last three carousels reached 189, 87 and 78 (Nov 20). The Nov 20 caption tagged none of the six people or companies it named and reused the first line of Oct 30 word for word, against the style guide's rules to tag every brand and vary the first line. For the next Movers post (due Dec 4), write a new first line, tag every person and company named on Instagram, invite the company of the lead move as collaborator and ask it to accept. Keep the LinkedIn post as it is.
next_step: Measure: Instagram reach after seven days against 87, the median of the last three Instagram Movers posts (Oct 16 to Nov 20); LinkedIn clicks against 89 (Nov 19).
